prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: தமிழ் / বাংলা · Mixed Indic (language ta).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "மொழி" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 46px
  col 2: header "ভাষা" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "பேசுவோர்" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 68px
  col 4: header "குறிப்பு" · longest unbreakable word 113px · one-line width 461px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare languages across Tamil and Bengali names, speaker counts, and brief notes.","reading":"Readers scan each row from the two language names to the speaker count and note, and compare counts down the third column.","groups":["Columns 1 and 2 give the same language name in two scripts, so they should read as a pair.","Column 3 gives the comparable numeric measure; column 4 provides descriptive context."],"keep_intact":["Language names and script-specific characters","Speaker counts and their units","Unbreakable words in the notes where space permits"],"may_wrap":["Notes in column 4 can wrap at natural word boundaries; their longer text can determine row height.","Short headers or values can wrap where necessary, with the other cells sharing the resulting row height."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[67,61,89,142],"idea":"Keep the longest unbreakable content intact in every column and give the remaining space to the notes."},{"name":"B","widths":[62,56,82,159],"idea":"Give the notes more room by narrowing all three comparison columns, accepting tighter wrapping or overflow for their longest unbreakable content."},{"name":"C","widths":[70,65,75,149],"idea":"Give the paired language names comfortable widths and favor the notes over the speaker-count column, accepting a tight third-column header."}]}
